## Purpose
The vault tables: entries, the previous value versions kept for rollback, and the audit log.

## Responsibilities
- **`vault_secrets` (VaultSecret)**, workspace-scoped:
  - `workspace_id`, `id` (uuid hex);
  - `name`: unique and indexed. It is the key code reads, `kwargs["_secrets"][NAME]`;
  - `label`;
  - `kind`: api_key (the default), token, password, username, url, connection_string, client_id, client_secret, certificate, config or other;
  - `service`, `description`;
  - `sensitive` (default True), `tags` (JSON list);
  - `allowed_consumers` (JSON list; `[]` means any consumer);
  - `ciphertext`, `key_id`, `hint`, `version` (default 1), `disabled`, `expires_at`;
  - `value_changed_at`, `last_used_at`, `last_used_by`, `use_count`;
  - `origin`: settings, build, connector or import;
  - `origin_ref`, and the timestamps.
- **`vault_secret_versions` (VaultSecretVersion):** an int PK, secret_id (indexed), version, ciphertext, key_id, hint and created_at.
- **`vault_audit` (VaultAuditEvent)**, workspace-scoped:
  - an int PK and `at` (indexed);
  - `action`: create, update, set_value, rollback, reveal, delete, use, denied, missing, rotate_key or bind;
  - secret_id and secret_name;
  - `actor` (default "user");
  - `consumer`;
  - `outcome`: ok, denied or error;
  - `detail`.

## Key elements
See Responsibilities.

## Interactions
- Used by `vault/store.py`.
- `VaultSecret` and `VaultAuditEvent` are registered for workspace scoping in `auth/setup.py`.

## Error handling and edge cases
None.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **`name` is unique across the whole table, not per workspace.** Two workspaces cannot have an entry with the same name.
- **`vault_secret_versions` is not workspace-scoped.** It is reached only through its parent entry.

## How to rebuild this file
Declare the three classes with exactly these columns and defaults.
